stories.title: PML-N retains both Gujranwala's NA-77 and Sahiwal's PP-203, unofficial results show
summary: Notices were also issued to several PML-N lawmakers for alleged violations of the election code, mostly over visiting polling stations in the two constituencies.
Earlier in the day, Chief Election Commissioner Sikander Sultan Raja visited the provincial election chief’s office, where he was briefed on the polling process in both constituencies, ECP said.
Notices were also issued over alleged violations of the Code of Conduct to PML-N’s MNA Syeda Nosheen Iftikhar and MPA Hina Arshad Warraich for allegedly visiting polling stations.

stories.title: 'Misplaced over-smartness': Maryam removes Jhelum DC over exam postponement for her visit
summary: It is, therefore, requested that the examination be postponed and rescheduled for another suitable date to avoid any inconvenience to students and ensure the smooth conduct of both the examination and the VVIP visit”.
Eventually, Maryam posted on X that the Jhelum DC was being removed from his post with “immediate effect”.

Maryam also shared a second correspondence, dated Nov 6, by the then-Jhelum DC, who had advised the BISE chairperson to change one of the examination centres, Comprehensive Government School, in view of the “VVIP visit” and possible traffic congestion.

stories.title: Turkiye's President Erdogan, Azerbaijan counterpart vow unity after tensions
summary: Turkiye’s President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and Azerbaijan’s President Ilham Aliyev vowed on Sunday that their countries’ alliance would remain solid, in a show of unity aimed at overcoming a public rift between the close neighbours.
On Sunday, as Azerbaijan marked Victory Day commemorating a 2020 war with Armenia, Erdogan arrived in the country’s Fuzuli district, which Baku recaptured from Armenian forces six years ago.
Turkiye is also seeking to normalise relations with Armenia, whose border it closed in the 1990s in solidarity with Azerbaijan, while linking progress to Armenian-Azerbaijani peace efforts.

stories.title: With Stephen Miller at the helm, Trump charts a course for confrontation
summary: The president also offered the job of White House press secretary to combat sports promoter Dana White. ‘This man saved America’ Miller, 41, marks a sharp contrast with outgoing chief of staff Susie Wiles, a former lobbyist who ran Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign.
Miller joined Trump’s first presidential campaign in 2016 and served throughout his two terms in the White House.
Miller has also overseen Trump’s executive orders, giving him an expansive understanding of the administrative tools available to the president.

stories.title: Eisenkot says Israel in 'devastating diplomatic crisis' as he seeks to form govt
summary: Israel’s former military chief Gadi Eisenkot started the tough task on Sunday of forming a government, reaching out to Benjamin Netanyahu’s allies as he warned the veteran prime minister had brought the country to a historic crisis.
Both Eisenkot and Netanyahu say Israeli troops will not withdraw from Gaza until Hamas ​is disarmed, and that Israel is prepared to ​restart fighting to achieve this.

Potentially making Eisenkot’s job tougher is the position of one opposition leader, Avigdor Lieberman of the Israel Our Home party, who has ruled out a unity government with Netanyahu or a minority government that has backing from Arab parties.

stories.title: Train collision in Egypt's Giza kills 4, injures 88: health ministry
summary: Egypt’s railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan.
Authorities said they had launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, which occurred in Giza’s Al-Ayyat area, the site of Egypt’s worst-ever rail disaster.
Egypt’s 110 million people depend heavily on rail transport, but the network — one of the largest in Africa — has suffered repeated deadly accidents.

stories.title: Trump says elections were 'giant step back in history' for US
summary: United States President Donald Trump vowed on Sunday to bounce back stronger from a massive midterm elections loss that he called a “giant step back in history” for the US.
It will be the first time that Trump, a Republican who also held the White House from 2017 to 2021, has had to contend with a Democratic-controlled Congress in both chambers.

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries has said the incoming majority will be focused on affordability and accountability. “We don’t work for Donald Trump,” the New York lawmaker told reporters on Wednesday. “We work for the American people.

stories.title: Husband held, investigation launched after anchorperson shot dead at Rawalpindi home
summary: In a statement, City Police Officer (CPO) Hassan Mushtaq Sukhera said Ahsan’s husband was taken into custody and the suspected weapon was seized.
The First Lady noted that the outcome of the investigation into Hina’s case was still awaited.

According to a DNA analysis report, DNA samples of Hina’s domestic servant matched postmortem swabs collected from her body, while her husband’s DNA also matched samples taken from multiple items at the crime scene.

stories.title: Aramco skyscraper damaged as Houthis target Riyadh financial district
summary: An Aramco building in Riyadh was targeted in an “attempted attack”, the Saudi energy ministry said on Sunday, with eyewitnesses telling AFP the skyscraper sustained damage, after the Saudi-led coalition fighting Houthis said it had intercepted missiles launched by the group.
Under the Makkah Defence Alliance, Pakistani, Saudi and Turkish leaders met in Riyadh and agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom.
The fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen’s capital Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.

stories.title: KP plans to set up faceless ATCs, spend Rs70bn on CTD and police in a year as part of counterterrorism initiatives
summary: Chairing his first apex committee meeting after taking charge of the province, governor Kundi promised to equip police and CTD with resources. “Whatever weapons you want, whatever you need, we will get them to you.

Governor Kundi calls for ownership of war against terrorism Speaking at the occasion, Governor Kundi said the provincial government’s priority was to restore peace and strengthen the police force, stressing that development would follow once security was ensured.

He said the police were at the forefront of the war against terrorism and needed to be adequately equipped to carry out their responsibilities. “Until we strengthen and facilitate [the police], how will they fight using just one Kalashnikov and a few bullets?” Kundi asked.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz, Nawaz discuss ‘matters of national importance’ as Sharifs gather at Lahore's Jati Umra
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif discussed matters of “national importance” with PML-N President Nawaz Sharif during a visit to the latter’s residence in Lahore’s Jati Umra on Sunday, state-run Radio Pakistan reported.
PM Shehbaz briefed the PML-N president on the law and order situation in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and on recent initiatives taken for the development and prosperity of the province, Radio Pakistan added.
The premier also apprised Nawaz of “the ongoing economic reforms by the government, the challenges being faced and the measures being taken to address them”, the outlet said.

stories.title: Hamza Zahoor’s unbeaten century guides Pakistan U-19 to thrilling win over India
summary: Hamza Zahoor produced a match-winning unbeaten century as Pakistan Under-19 defeated arch-rivals India by three wickets in a thrilling Group ‘A’ encounter of the ACC Men’s Under-19 Asia Cup at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Muscat on Sunday.
Pakistan’s chase, however, was far from straightforward as India’s bowlers made early inroads to reduce them to 61 for five.
However, the right-hander received little support from the other end as Pakistan’s bowlers maintained pressure and regularly picked up wickets to restrict India to a modest total.

stories.title: SAFF Championship: Pakistan cruise past Maldives 3-0, close in on semi-final spot
summary: A first-half brace from Najeebullah Bettani, alongside an early penalty converted by McKeal Aroon Abdullah, helped Pakistan register their first victory of the tournament and put themselves in a strong position to qualify for the last four.

With their victory over Maldives, Pakistan have moved into a stronger position in the qualification race but must now wait for the outcome of the remaining Group ‘B’ fixture between India and Maldives, scheduled for Nov 11.
Maldives will need a substantial victory over India to overtake Pakistan in the group standings and secure qualification.

stories.title: Train collision in Egypt kills at least 7, injures dozens, health ministry says
summary: Two passenger trains collided some 76 km (47 ‌miles) south of Cairo on Sunday, killing at least seven people and injuring 112, Egypt’s health ministry said.
Emergency crews were clearing the wreckage to restore ​services on the Cairo-Upper Egypt line, the railway authority said, without giving any indication of how long this would ​take.
In the country's worst-ever rail disaster, a fire tore through seven carriages of an ⁠overcrowded ​passenger service in 2002, killing ​at least 360 people.

stories.title: Husband, relative arrested after woman allegedly electrocuted to death in Okara
summary: A woman was allegedly tortured and electrocuted to death by her husband, with the help of his sister, brother-in-law and nephew, in Ahmed Nagar within the jurisdiction of Cantt police station.

According to Okara DPO spokesperson Irfan Sandhu Jutt, Cantt police received information that Misbah's sudden death was not natural and that she had allegedly been murdered by her husband, Tanveer, in collusion with his relatives.
When police reached the scene, Tanveer allegedly fled.

stories.title: Türkiye supports Azerbaijan's efforts for lasting peace in South Caucasus: Erdogan
summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan on Sunday reaffirmed Türkiye's support for Azerbaijan's efforts to establish lasting peace in the South Caucasus, saying the liberation of Karabakh had opened the door to a new era in the region.

Azerbaijan-Türkiye unity 'eternal and unshakable' For his part, Aliyev expressed gratitude for Türkiye's support during the 44-day Second Karabakh War, emphasizing that Azerbaijan would never forget the solidarity demonstrated by Erdogan and the Turkish people.

Aliyev noted that the Second Karabakh War had once again demonstrated the unity between Türkiye and Azerbaijan, recalling that the Shusha Declaration formally elevated bilateral relations to the level of an alliance.

stories.title: ‘Special connection with Pakistan’: US Senator Van Hollen, eyeing 2028 presidential bid, was born in Karachi
summary: US Democrat Senator Christopher Van Hollen, who has set his sights on the 2028 contest for the American presidential office, was born in Karachi.

I am fortunate to have a special connection with Pakistan, having been born in Karachi as the son of an American foreign service officer. “Throughout my life, I have experienced first-hand the generosity, the goodness and the determination of the Pakistani people.
In 2021, Van Hollen had thanked Pakistan among other countries for helping evacuate American nationals and others stranded in Afghanistan following the Taliban takeover of the country.

stories.title: RETHINKING PAKISTAN’S AUTO POLICY
summary: An auto policy cannot run provincial bus services, but it can reduce fleet costs and make public support conditional on affordable service.

Under these assumptions, monthly costs per commuter are roughly Rs1,900 for a bus, Rs4,900 for an electric motorcycle, Rs5,200 for wagons and rickshaws, Rs7,000 for a petrol motorcycle and Rs39,900 for a small petrol car.
In my model, an electric bus running around 70,000 kilometres a year with 800 passenger boardings a day needs about Rs21.5 million in annual public support if borrowing costs 18 percent.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz raises youth loan limit to Rs25m under business, agriculture schemes
summary: The decision was taken at a meeting chaired by the prime minister to review the disbursement of loans to young people and the implementation of the two schemes.

The prime minister directed the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Authority (SMEDA) to provide all possible assistance to young people under the schemes, including guidance on starting businesses, business consultancy and technical support.
During the 2026-27 financial year, an estimated 266,700 young people are expected to receive loans worth Rs292b under the schemes, the meeting was told.

stories.title: Siblings acquitted in blasphemy case after 20 years
summary: The brothers, Liaqat Ali and Umar Draz, have spent around 20 years behind bars.

In the light of the opinion of medical board which raises doubts regarding the culpability of the appellants, the benefit of doubt cannot be withheld from the appellants,” the judgement said.

stories.title: Former Israeli premier urges Eisenkot to swiftly replace Netanyahu government
summary: Barak said he would welcome Arab parties joining the next government.
On Saturday, Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced that he would task Eisenkot with forming the next government.
Under Israel’s Basic Law, Eisenkot will have 28 days to form a government once he receives the mandate.

stories.title: Broken record: Pakistan struggles with refugee influx; US supports Iran against the Soviet Union
summary: As Pakistan took its first few steps, the massive logistical task of accommodating millions of refugees in the midst of widespread communal violence was a major challenge for the state.
But Urdu and Pakistan are joined at the hip, and as the issue of Sept 9 noted, the formation of the Urdu Anjuman was a major event in the nation’s cultural history.

The initial meeting was held in Karachi’s YMCA Hall on Sept 8 “under the Presidentship of Pir Illahi Bakhsh”, Sind’s education minister. “The organisation will serve as a nucleus for the propagation of Urdu throughout Pakistan,” the report said.

stories.title: At least 21 dead after migrant boat sinks off Senegal coast, government says
summary: At least 21 people have ​died after a boat carrying ‌migrants sank off the Senegalese coast, the interior ministry said on Sunday.
Search and ​rescue operations were continuing as ​authorities looked for possible additional survivors The boat ‌was ⁠carrying people seeking to migrate irregularly, the statement said.

It did not say how many ​were on ​board Thousands of ⁠people have died in recent years attempting to ​reach Spain's Canary Islands ​from ⁠West Africa, including 635 in the first five months of this ⁠year, ​according to migrant ​rights group Walking Borders.

stories.title: Anchorperson shot dead at home in Rawalpindi, husband arrested
summary: An anchorperson, Rabia Ahsan, was allegedly shot dead by her husband at their home in Rawalpindi, with police taking the suspect into custody and seizing the weapon used in the incident.
Senior anchorperson Absa Komal said she was heartbroken over the death of Rabia, describing her as a respected anchor, dedicated journalist and mother.
Heartbroken by the tragic death of Rabia Ahsan, a respected anchor, dedicated journalist and mother.

stories.title: How China’s clean-tech machine is reshaping the global climate fight
summary: China sent $132 billion in clean technology and investment to the developing world last year, by far the largest contribution to carbon-dioxide reduction of any country.

The $132 billion figure derived by Reuters for China’s global climate contribution also includes an estimated $40 billion of Chinese foreign direct investment into clean-technology projects in developing countries.

That brings China’s contribution to nearly equal to the $137 billion in climate finance that wealthy nations provided to poorer ones in 2024 under their UN climate pledges, according to the most recent figures provided by the OECD.

stories.title: Pakistan edge India to reach Under-19 Asia Cup semi-finals
summary: Hamza Zahoor struck an unbeaten century to guide Pakistan Under-19s to a thrilling three-wicket victory over India and secure their place in the semi-finals of the Asian Cricket Council (ACC) Under-19 Asia Cup on Sunday.
Chasing 209 at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman, Pakistan achieved the target with 11 balls to spare with Zahoor producing a match-winning 100 not out off 108 deliveries to steer his side home.
Rajput held India's innings together despite losing partners at the other end, but Pakistan's bowlers kept striking to prevent the visitors from building a bigger total.

stories.title: Can't cook or shower: Indonesians take aim at data centres
summary: Recent disruption to water distribution "was not caused by data centres or AI or investors entering that sector," Amsakar Achmad, Batam mayor and head of BP Batam said in October, according to local media.
AFP The government said at that time it would only approve data centre projects after ensuring sufficient energy and water supply capacity.
Data centres "use a lot of water," the retiree told AFP, adding that, as in Batam, "if the rain doesn't come for one month, we all feel it".

stories.title: Pakistan whip Maldives to stay alive in SAFF Cup
summary: Pakistan moved closer to securing a place in the semi-finals after producing a dominant 3-0 victory over Maldives in their second Group B match of the SAFF Cup at National Stadium Dhaka on Sunday.

Collecting a clearance on the right after Pakistan had defended deep in their own half, Bettani brought the ball under control before unleashing a powerful strike beyond the helpless Maldives goalkeeper.
Pakistan must now await the outcome of the remaining Group match between the Maldives and India to confirm their semi-final qualification.

stories.title: Babar Azam says selection not in his hands as youthful Pakistan face Sri Lanka
summary: Babar’s remarks come as Pakistan prepare to field a considerably revamped side following their disappointing performance in the previous phase of the World Test Championship (WTC).

The hosts defeated Sri Lanka in the final of the ODI tri-series towards the end of October, and Babar believes the result has helped lift the team’s confidence. “Any series or match you win gives you confidence, and we have brought that vibe into the Test matches.
Sri Lanka’s last series victory against Pakistan came in the UAE in 2017, while Pakistan won their most recent encounter 2-0 in Sri Lanka in 2023.

stories.title: Electric auto rickshaws reshape India's roads
summary: Every 90 seconds, an electric three-wheeler rolls off the production line at an Indian factory, underscoring a transformation that has made the country the largest market for battery-powered auto rickshaws.
"Rickshaws, which operate continuously throughout the day, accumulate fuel savings rapidly," said Bidisha Bhattacharya of the Delhi-based Chintan Research Foundation.
Climate think-tank Ember said India consumes less transport fuel per capita than China did at a comparable income level in 2012, helped by the spread of cheap solar power and declining battery costs.

stories.title: Democrats planning flood of AI bills when they take control of Congress
summary: Democrats are planning to unleash a flood of new legislation targeting artificial intelligence systems and data-center development when they take control of the US Congress in January, lawmakers, congressional aides and advocates said.

Democrats plan on introducing bills aimed at shielding consumers from rising electricity costs tied to data centers, requiring independent testing of advanced AI systems and clarifying when AI companies can be held liable for harm caused by their products, they said.

Most US voters think ​Trump's administration and Congress are not taking the risks of AI seriously enough and want the government to write new ​regulations for the technology, ⁠according to a Reuters poll published in October.

stories.title: Trump orders US Justice Department to look into Democrats for 'threatening' people with impeachment, other penalties
summary: President Donald Trump ordered the US Justice Department on Saturday to look into Democrats for “threatening a lot of people” with impeachment and other ​forms of punishment, saying in a social media post that their actions amount ‌to a “criminal act”, without providing evidence.
Republican Senator Mike Lee of Utah wrote on social media that Slotkin was threatening young people who wanted to go into politics.
Trump’s Justice Department ⁠has investigated Slotkin before.

stories.title: Hodge's ton puts West Indies in command against Bangladesh in second Test
summary: Kavem Hodge hit an unbeaten 140 to extend West Indies' lead to 315 on the fourth day of the second Test against Bangladesh in Sylhet on Sunday.
West Indies reached 345-3 in their second innings when bad light halted play, with Hodge hitting 17 fours and a six off 189 balls and Amir Jangoo also unbeaten on 20.
Hodge said he was pleased to contribute after failing to convert a start in the first Test in Dhaka, adding that the West Indies would assess conditions before deciding when to declare.

stories.title: PM Shehbaz briefs Nawaz Sharif on K-P security, economic challenges
summary: According to the PMO, the meeting took place at Jati Umra, where Nawaz was briefed on the government’s ongoing reforms, particularly economic reforms, the challenges facing the country and measures being taken to address them.

Under the proclamation, the provincial chief minister, cabinet members, advisers and advocate general ceased to hold office, while the governor assumed powers assigned to him by the federal government.

At a briefing in Peshawar on Saturday, Governor Faisal Karim Kundi said the provincial government had planned Rs70 billion for the police and Rs10.3 billion for the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) during the current financial year.

stories.title: Usman Khawaja denies throwing 'anyone under the bus' with comments about Australia's 2018 ball-tampering scandal
summary: Usman Khawaja insisted on Sunday he did not “throw anyone under the bus” by claiming the entire Australian team was in on the 2018 “Sandpapergate” plot and defended taking eight years to go public.

That probe found only Smith, Warner and Bancroft were in the know. “When I mentioned it was all of us, that’s implying that whether we like it or not, we’re all responsible for what happened together as a team,” Khawaja said in a lengthy Instagram post on Sunday.

That’s the first time I tried to come out.” Khawaja said he again almost spoke up in 2021 when bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon all denied publicly that they knew about the ball-tampering.

stories.title: Bomb Disposal Squad official martyred as IED goes off in KP's South Waziristan
summary: SOUTH WAZIRISTAN: An assistant head of the police’s Bomb Disposal Squad (BDS) was martyred after an improvised explosive device (IED) went off in the Janta area of Sararogha tehsil in Upper South Waziristan district on Saturday while he was attempting to defuse it.

Upper South Waziristan district police officer (DPO) Ashfaq Khan told Dawn that the official, identified as Abdul Jabbar, was busy defusing the IED when an explosion occurred, leaving him seriously injured.

On the same day, an incident was reported in Toi Khulla Bazaar in Lower South Waziristan district, where an unidentified person wearing a burqa threw a hand grenade near the place where police personnel were seated.

stories.title: PTI's Gohar demands end to ‘political victimisation’
summary: SWAT: Pakistan Tehreek-i-Insaf Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan on Saturday called for judicial independence, rule of law and an end to what he described as political victimisation.
The PTI chairman said that access to party founder Imran Khan, including meetings with his personal physician and family members, remained their foremost demand.
Describing political isolation and what he termed “political apartheid” as harmful to democracy, Barrister Khan expressed concern over the alleged illegal detention of political leaders.

stories.title: Pak-Afghan trade cannot proceed amid terrorism: Samar Haroon Bilour
summary: She said the reopening of trade routes depended on addressing Pakistan’s legitimate security concerns and securing practical cooperation from the Afghan authorities.

She urged Kabul to ensure that its territory was not used by militant groups to carry out attacks against Pakistan. “The threat of terrorism persists, but the law and order situation in the province has improved,” the governor’s adviser said in a statement issued by her office.
The governor’s adviser also confirmed that Pakistan’s national flag had been hoisted on government buildings and offices in the areas concerned.

stories.title: Governor invites Chinese investors to explore KP’s potential
summary: The meeting, attended by a delegation of Chinese investors, focused on investment opportunities in the province, particularly in the minerals sector, as well as the potential for investment in its economic zones, according to a statement issued by the governor’s office.

He said the province faced enormous challenges, including terrorism, displacement and prolonged instability, which had placed additional pressure on the healthcare system and other essential public services, according to another statement issued by the governor’s office.

The governor said people deserved a healthcare system that served them with dignity, empathy and responsibility and that professional organisations such as the Pakistan Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons could play a significant role in improving healthcare services.

stories.title: Joint investigation team formed to probe violent clashes after court hearing in Sindh's Kotri
summary: Another person, Azeem Barejo, who was injured during the scuffle, was taken to the Liaquat University Hospital, Jamshoro, by his brother, Dhani Bakhsh, who had proceeded to the court after hearing about the scuffle.
The FIR was lodged against Dhani Bakhsh, his son Sarmad and brothers, Azeem, Aslam, Sharif and Ismail.
The court hearing on Friday pertained to an application for confirmation or otherwise of a pre-arrest bail filed by Azeem, his brother Sharif and their nephew Sarmad (son of Dhani Bakhsh).
